summary: With Any Kind, the kind a search starts with, and with Kind: Folder, a token with a slash at an end that stands beside other tokens (`/notes/ todo`, `todo notes/`, `todo /notes`, `!notes/ todo`) is now fff-search's folder filter (PathSegment, the one the file kinds already use) instead of one more fuzzy word: the folder's name must match whole, at any depth inside the search location, with letter case ignored from A to Z, and it can name folders in a row. `search_root` in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs parses those two searches with a ParserConfig of fffinder's own, `WithFolders`, which equals fff-search's DirSearchConfig / MixedSearchConfig except that its `parse_custom` returns the filter; a glob with a slash at an end is still a glob. A folder token that is the whole search (`src/`, `/notes/`, `!src/`), in one folder or everywhere, parses as before. In Any Kind every token that ends in a slash now goes before the others, so two at the end no longer give folders only. A filter reaches fff-search as typed in `search` and in `track_open`, so a search with one still remembers what was opened from it. docs/manual.md has a new paragraph on folder filters.
changelog: Folder filters didn't filter in the searches most people run. With **Any Kind**, the kind a search starts with, and with **Folder**, `/notes/ todo` and `todo notes/` took the folder for one more fuzzy word, so they also listed `meeting-notes/todo.txt` and `other/notes-todo.txt`. Only a search for one kind of file, such as Document, kept to the folder. A folder filter beside other words now keeps to what is inside a folder with exactly that name, whatever the kind. The name must match whole, with letter case ignored from A to Z. `!notes/` leaves out only what is inside a folder named `notes`; it used to leave out every path with `notes/` in it, `meeting-notes/` included. Two of them at the end, as in `readme projects/ !atlas/`, no longer turn the results into folders only. A folder filter that is the whole search, such as `src/`, still lists the folders that match it, and globs work as before. `fff find` follows the same rules.
behaviour_changes: All of these are for searches with folders in the results: the window with Any Kind or Kind: Folder, Smart Folders and the file chooser with those kinds, and `fff find` without `--files` or with `--dirs`. Searches for one kind of file, `fff find --files`, `fff files` and `fff dirs` return what they did. I compared 25 searches the change must leave alone (no slash token, a file kind, files only, or a lone folder token) on a tree of 818 crates, trunk against changed code: same counts and same scores; the items that differ at the tail differ the same way between two runs of one binary (fff-search's cut among equal scores).

A token that starts or ends with `/`, beside at least one other token, is a folder filter: only items inside a folder with exactly that name, at any depth inside the search location. `/notes/ todo`, `todo notes/`, `todo /notes` and `/NOTES/ todo` list only what is inside `notes`; the trunk also listed `meeting-notes/todo-agenda.txt`, `other/notes-todo.txt` and more. In the demo folder `rs src/` went from 26 items to 3 and `json product/` from 5 to 1.
The name must match whole. `tax /tax/` no longer lists the folder `Tax [2026]`; `todo notes2/` no longer lists anything in `notes`; `todo archive/` no longer lists `todo-archive` and what is in it.

The folder a filter names counts as inside it. It is listed when its own path matches the words (`rs src/` in the demo folder lists lib.rs, main.rs and the folder `src`; `items todo-items/` lists that folder and the file in it), and `!notes/` leaves the folder out with what it holds. fff-search stores a folder's path with a slash at its end, which is why. The test pins it.

Letter case is ignored from A to Z only. `Todo /Notes2/` and `todo notes2/` both find `Notes2/Todo.txt`. A lowercase filter no longer finds a folder with a capital outside A to Z: `todo /über/` found `Über/todo.txt` on the trunk (as a fuzzy word) and finds nothing now; `todo /Über/` finds it. The manual says so.
A filter can name folders in a row: `main lib/src/`, `first /notes/todo-items/`, `list /src/finder/`.

`!notes/` and `!/notes/` beside other tokens leave out a folder named `notes` and what is inside it, and nothing else. On the trunk `!notes/` left out every path containing `notes/` (so `meeting-notes/…` too) and `!/notes/` left out nothing at the top of a search location. `main !src/` now also lists `mysrc/main.rs`.
Kind: Folder: `todo notes/` lists only `notes/todo-items`; the trunk also listed `other/todo-archive`.

Any Kind: two or more tokens ending in `/` at the end no longer give folders only when another token is there. `todo notes/ !other/` listed only the folder `todo-items`; it now lists the files as well. `readme !atlas/ projects/` in the demo folder: No Results before, `Projects/beacon/README.md` now. `lib /SRC/ !tests/` in the crates tree listed unrelated folders before and lists the lib.rs files in src now.

Allow typos: turning it off made no difference to the loose results on the trunk (`/notes/ todo` 7 hits, `todo notes/` 9, in my fixture); the filtered results are the same with it on or off (4 and 4).

Ranking: a filter no longer counts toward a result's score, so the order inside the folder can differ (`file many/` in the demo folder now starts with file-001; the trunk started with file-065). With a filter and no word left (`notes/ *.md`) every result has fff-search's frecency score, 0 in a fresh index.

While typing: after another word, a filter that starts with a slash finds nothing until its name is complete. `readme /p` … `readme /project` show No Results (4, 4, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 items on the trunk), then `readme /projects` shows the 2 filtered items. Typing the filter first (`/projects/ readme`) or last in the trailing form (`readme projects/`) has no empty step. The file kinds already behaved this way.

A folder with a space in its name can't be a filter, because a filter is one token: `brand guidelines/` and `brand guidelines/ logo` listed the folder `Brand guidelines` and its files on the trunk (two fuzzy words) and list nothing now, in Any Kind and in Kind: Folder. `brand guidelines` without the slash finds the folder as before, and the manual gives the glob that stands in for the filter, `**/Brand?guidelines/** colors`.

A path pasted beside a word (`/Users/me/Documents report`, `~/notes/ todo`, `./notes/ todo`, `C:/Users/ x`) is a filter and finds nothing unless that chain of folders is inside the search location. A search location's own name is not in the paths, so `todo fx/` in a location named fx finds nothing (the trunk listed everything matching todo, because a three-letter fuzzy word with two typos allowed matches any path with a slash). A pasted path alone is still a fuzzy word.
A search of slash-ending tokens only (`notes/ docs/`) is still folders only in Any Kind, and now lists exactly the folders inside both; the trunk listed loosely matching folders.

Search memory: a search with a folder filter is remembered with the filter as typed (`/Docs/ readme`), where the trunk stored it in lowercase. An entry stored by an earlier version for a filter typed with a capital no longer counts until the file is opened again; one typed in lowercase still does.

Unchanged, and pinned by the new test: a lone `notes/` lists folders only and fuzzily (it still lists `meeting-notes`); a lone folder token in a search of one folder is still a word; a glob with a slash at an end (`archive oth*/`, `todo */notes/`) is still a glob; extensions beside a filter are still alternatives (`/notes/ *.md *.txt`).

Speed, the implementer's figures (debug build, 30,000 files): `main src/` 19.8 ms before, 12.6 ms now; `todo /notes/` 20.5 to 15.6 ms; `todo notes/ !src/` 1.9 ms (folders only) to 15.9 ms (files too). I did not measure it again. Nothing in my runs was slow: 25 searches over a tree of 818 crates, indexing included, took 1.1 s with the change.

Manual: one new paragraph at the end of Search syntax (not fuzzy, whole name, any depth inside the search location, `!notes/`, A to Z, folders in a row, no space and the glob to use instead, alone it is a word with Any Kind or Folder). The syntax table, the Search Syntax dialog and README are unchanged and now true for every kind.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

`Engine::list`, that is `fff dirs [query]` and GET /v1/dirs, still reads folder tokens as fuzzy words (DirSearchConfig). The brief is about `search_root`, and the manual promises search syntax only for `fff find`. `fff files` already filters. See Found, not fixed.
A search made only of tokens that end in `/` (`notes/ docs/`, `notes/ !docs/`) is still folders only in Any Kind, as on the trunk.
A lone `!src/` is unchanged, as the plan says: a substring exclusion and, in Any Kind, folders only.
Letter case beyond A to Z: fff-search compares those letters as typed, so `/über/` does not match a folder named `Über`. Not worked around; the manual says so.
The list is not kept from going empty while a filter that starts with a slash is typed after a word (`todo /no`). The plan accepted it and the file kinds do the same.

No fallback to fuzzy words when a filter names no folder. It would bring back `meeting-notes/todo.txt` for `/notes/ todo` wherever there is no folder named notes, which is what the manual says doesn't happen.

The opened-before boost is still missed when the filter is written at the end, because moving it changes the text fff-search looks the search up under. That was so before; the brief query-history-boost is about it.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing under src/term changed and no signature it calls changed (grep for the changed names in src/ is empty).
Only Linux was compiled and run. No platform-specific code was touched. The second new test is `#[cfg(not(windows))]`, like the test above it and for the same reason.
No headless UI test: the change is all in the engine. The window was looked at through screenshots, by the implementer and by me.
tests: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs: engine::tests::folder_filters_narrow_searches_that_can_list_folders (after quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter). Fails without the change: with the trunk's code above `mod tests` and this commit's test module, it stops at its first assertion with left ["first.md", "notes-todo.txt", "todo-agenda.txt", "todo-items", "todo.txt"], right ["first.md", "todo-items", "todo.txt"]. By the implementer's count eight of its searches give the wrong result on the trunk; the others guard what must not change (Kind Document, folders in a row, the Cyrillic folder, a lone `notes/`, a scoped lone `archive/`, the glob `archive oth*/`, and the two added in review).

crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs: engine::tests::a_search_with_a_folder_filter_remembers_what_it_opened (after a_search_remembers_what_it_opened_whatever_the_capitals; not compiled on Windows, like that test). A guard: it passes on the trunk. I saw it fail (README.md first where readme.md is expected) with `track_open` folding folder tokens as words again, and with `search` doing so.
review_fixes: Test: two assertions pin that the folder a filter names counts as inside it (`items todo-items/` with Any Kind lists the folder and the file in it; `todo !todo-items/` with Kind: Folder leaves the folder out). The brief's risks asked the test to pin this either way, and nothing did: `rs src/` in the demo folder lists the folder `src` beside its two files.

docs/manual.md, the new paragraph: `!notes/` 'leaves out only a folder with that name and what is inside it' (it read 'only what is inside', and the folder goes too), and one sentence more: a filter can't have a space in it, with the glob to use for such a folder, `**/Brand?guidelines/** colors`. I ran that glob in the demo folder with Any Kind and Document, in both letter cases. Without it the first thing a filter meets on a Mac, a folder name of two words, gives No Results with nothing to say why.
Commit message: the two points above, in the paragraphs they belong to.

Rebased onto 7ef1f95 (results-scroll-reset), 595ce0f (scope-chips-keep-focus) and 40f8e86 (search-truncation-honesty), which landed during the review. No conflicts. 40f8e86 changed the end of `Engine::search` (cut_to_limit, `truncated`) and the content search; this change is in the head of `search`, in `search_root` and in `track_open`, and the two don't meet. check.sh was run on the result.

Nothing else was changed. The engine code is the implementer's; I agree with both of its deviations from the plan (parse_custom in place of enable_path_segments, which keeps `archive oth*/` a glob, and the reorder as a stable sort, without which `todo notes/ !other/` is folders only).
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit after the rebase: 524 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. Pushed to origin (40f8e86..82f79a2).

How it was checked. I put the trunk's engine code above this commit's test module: folder_filters_narrow_searches_that_can_list_folders fails at its first assertion, and the memory test passes, as the implementer said; it is a guard, and it fails under the two mutations I ran (`track_open` folding folder tokens as words, `search` doing so). Trunk and changed code were then run side by side through a small probe (an example built in the lane and removed again) on a 24-file fixture, the demo folder and a tree of 818 crates: about 170 searches by hand, each compared. 2,400 generated searches (one or two words, one or two filters in the three spellings, some negated, some in capitals, Any Kind and Folder, four scopes) were checked against a model written apart from the engine: no result outside a folder its filters name or inside one they leave out, and nothing the model expects was missing except where every word is a single letter (see Found, not fixed). Typing was simulated letter by letter for eight searches. I took three screenshots of my own (light and dark).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) No Results where there were results, with nothing to say why. Four cases, all from the filter being exact: a filter that starts with a slash, half typed after a word; a folder name with a space; a lowercase filter for a name with a capital outside A to Z; a pasted path beside a word. Each is the documented meaning and what the file kinds already did, and the plan accepted three of them. The fourth, the space, is now in the manual with the glob that replaces it. I did not add a fallback to fuzzy words: for `/notes/ todo` with no folder named notes it would list `meeting-notes/todo.txt` again.
(2) Folders only where files were wanted. fff-search searches folders only when the text it is given ends in a slash. The token sort moves every slash-ending token to the front, so that happens only when every token ends in one; in a search of one folder the folder's glob is last. Checked with `todo notes/`, `todo notes/ !other/`, `!notes/ todo` and three tokens in both orders.
(3) A search that forgets what was opened from it, or boosts the wrong file. `search` and `track_open` fold with the same rule (filters as typed beside other tokens, a lone folder token in lowercase), and the guard test fails when either drifts. The search made as typed keeps the same filters, so its union with the lowercase search is sound.

Doubts for the owner.
1. The empty list while `todo /no` is typed. It is transient and the file kinds do it, but it is the one place where the default search got worse to type. Reading only tokens that end in a slash as filters would smooth it for Any Kind and Folder, at the price of `/notes x` meaning one thing with Document and another with Any Kind; `fuzzy_text` and `fold_word_case` would have to follow.
2. Lowercase filters and capitals outside A to Z (`/über/`, `/москва/` for `Москва`). For someone whose folder names are not in Latin letters, every filter has to be typed with its capital. fff-search's PathSegment compares bytes; working around it needs the folder's real spelling from the index.
3. The folder itself counting as inside. Both the brief and its verifier called either outcome acceptable; it is what fff-search does, it makes `!notes/` drop the folder as one would expect, and it is pinned now. Leaving the folder out of the positive case would need the engine to check folder hits itself.
4. Only Linux was run. The first new test runs on Windows and macOS in CI; it compares names only, creates one Cyrillic folder name, and uses the scoped search that searches_a_folder already runs there.

For briefs still to come.
- scoped-search-special-folder-names: the Any Kind and Folder branches of `search_root` now parse with `WithFolders { only, folder_filters }`, not MixedSearchConfig / DirSearchConfig; push your `Constraint::Glob` onto what `QueryParser::new(config).parse(&query)` returns there. `Constraint` is already imported. `folder_filters` comes from `folder_tokens_filter(user)`, the user's tokens, so it stays right when the scope glob no longer joins the query text; the comment above it ("`query` may have the searched folder's glob in it by now") then goes stale. Without the glob at its end, a scoped Any Kind search of several tokens that ends in a slash token ends in `/` and relies on the token sort, which must keep running on the final `query`. The first new test's scoped assertion only asks for the folder `todo-archive` among the hits of a lone `archive/`, so it holds when that search becomes folders only. A filter's names are matched from the search location down, not from the searched folder, so inside a folder named notes `todo notes/` lists everything matching todo.
- query-history-boost: `search` and `track_open` both compute `typed` and then `fold_word_case(&typed, … !folder_tokens_filter(&typed))`: beside other tokens a filter is kept as typed, alone it is lowercased as a word. The guard test pins `/Docs/ README`: open readme.md from it and it comes first the next time. If you key by a `history_key` of the typed text on both sides, that test should still pass. A filter ignores case from A to Z, so `/Docs/ x` and `/docs/ x` are one search under two keys today; lowercasing A to Z in filter tokens of the key would merge them and keep entries earlier versions wrote. The token sort still changes fff-search's raw_query for a search that ends in a slash token.
- kind-filter-single-list: `Constraint` is already in the import list. The file kinds still parse with `QueryParser::default()`, where a lone `/notes/` is a filter only because the kind's extensions make the search more than one token (fff-search turns a lone PathSegment into text). If a kind ever sends no extension tokens, that changes.
- typo-fallback-near-miss: `words` still leaves folder tokens out. Beside other tokens they are exact filters now, so nothing loose comes from them. A lone folder token (`notes/`) is a fuzzy word the strict check never sees: it lists `other/` with Allow typos on or off. If your near-miss check should cover it, the word is the token without its slashes.
- empty-state-messages: No Results is now what a folder filter that names no folder gives with Any Kind and Folder too: `brand guidelines/ logo`, `todo /no` while it is typed, `/über/ x` for `Über`. SearchResponse has nothing that tells these apart from a search that simply found nothing; a detail line such as "No folder named …" would need the engine to say so.
- search-syntax-click-example: the examples `/notes/ todo` and `main src/` filter exactly with Any Kind now. In a folder with no folder named notes or src (the demo folder has `Projects/atlas/src` but no notes) the first gives No Results where it gave loose matches, so assert on the search field's text or use a fixture that has `notes/`.
- result-tie-break, sorted-search-results: with a filter and no word (`notes/ *.md`) every hit has the same score, so your order decides the whole list there. `rerank` is untouched.
- multi-word-highlights, live-search-results, recents-walk-index, adhoc-index-feedback, search-settings-without-effect, regex-content-search (all in engine.rs): `fuzzy_text`, `words`, `rerank`, `highlight` and the content search are untouched. New in the file: `folder_tokens_filter` and `WithFolders` with its `impl ParserConfig`, between `fuzzy_text` and `split_quoted`; `fold_word_case`'s second parameter is now `folder_words`; the reorder in `search_root` is a four-line sort of the tokens; one test after quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter and one after a_search_remembers_what_it_opened_whatever_the_capitals.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: a saved search with a folder token beside words filters exactly from now on, so a Smart Folder that leaned on the loose match shows fewer items. Nothing to do in your change.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
- `fff dirs "todo notes/"` reads the folder token as a fuzzy word, while `fff files` filters. In `Engine::list`, `QueryParser::new(WithFolders { only: true, folder_filters: folder_tokens_filter(q) })` and `fold_word_case(q, dirs && !folder_tokens_filter(q))` would bring it in line, and DirSearchConfig would leave the imports.
- A search whose words are all single letters lists no files: fff-search matches no file when no word has two letters, and lists every folder. `t a` gives folders only on the trunk. With this change `notes/ t a` joins it (the trunk had `notes/` as a word to match), as the file kinds already did; `notes/ t` and `notes/ t ab` are fine.
- With Any Kind, a search made only of slash-ending tokens is folders only (`notes/ !docs/`), a lone `!src/` is a substring exclusion and folders only, and a lone `src/` in a search of one folder lists files too.
- A token with a colon (`todo:12`, a line suffix) is left out of `words`, so the strict check never looks at it and its typo matches stay: `notes/ todo:12` lists everything in notes.
- A search location's own name never satisfies a filter, in any kind, because paths are taken inside the location.
- `main /` puts the bare `/` first, and fff-search takes its first text part as the main needle.
- `git stash` is one list shared by every lane's worktree (the implementer saw another lane's entry). The guide's `git stash -u` advice can hand one lane another lane's stash. I did not use it.
